one_line: Voice- and WebMCP-controlled 3D chess with an AI teacher.
what_it_does: Lets players learn and play chess through voice, touch, mouse, or structured agent actions, with lessons and AI opponents.
leverage_rationale: Chess has exact board state and legal actions, making structured WebMCP access materially more reliable than pixel-driven UI automation; the claimed shared board/agent interaction is central.
leverage_evidence: About text claims 29 tools for moves, lessons, coaching, settings, saves, and replays.
Frames visibly show a rendered chessboard and game state, while the description says voice and WebMCP share game actions.
execution_rationale: The packet shows polished onboarding and a 3D board, but the submitted frame sheets are highly repetitive and do not show a move sequence or completed lesson/game workflow.
execution_evidence: Frames show Choose your path and a rendered 3D chessboard with pieces and controls.
Devpost screenshot shows a paused demo preview with a move/status message, not direct interaction.
impact_rationale: A clear audience of chess learners and players could benefit from conversational coaching and accessible voice control; the fit is credible though end-to-end coaching is not demonstrated.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets learning and playing chess with an AI master teacher.
About text claims six lessons, Stockfish opponents, ratings, trophies, saves, and replays.
creativity_rationale: A memorable synthesis of fantasy 3D chess, conversational tutoring, and agent-controlled exact board actions; ambition is strong for the scope.
creativity_evidence: Voice conversation is presented as the primary chess interaction.

leverage_rationale: Typed page tools can orchestrate review-board selection and results more reliably than UI automation, but the underlying review service already exists and the agent is mainly an orchestration layer.

About text says panel size is resolved server-side from plan/credit rather than passed by the agent.

impact_rationale: Decision-makers reviewing ADRs, policies, or design documents have a clear need for independent perspectives and preserved dissent; value is credible despite missing live evidence.
impact_evidence: About text names architecture decisions, policies, and design docs as artifacts.

creativity_rationale: The explicit separation between agent advice, spend recommendation, and human purchase decision is a thoughtful agent-commerce interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tagline frames the agent as convening the board while the human decides cost.
Server-side plan constraint is made part of the hackathon concept.
usability_note: Product page is coherent and readable; actual board flow is not shown.
red_flags: About text explicitly says the core product and paying customers predate the hackathon.
Embedded video unavailable; no direct tool execution evidence.
standouts: Preserved dissent and human-controlled spend boundary.
advance_reason: Interesting integration, but pre-existing core and absent runnable demo evidence weaken eligibility and execution.

one_line: Agent-assisted employment-contract review with human redline decisions.
what_it_does: Loads contracts, extracts and assesses clauses, proposes grounded redlines, and exports a negotiation email as the human accepts or rejects changes.
leverage_rationale: Clause-level structured reads and writes let an agent work precisely against document state; the human retains each consequential decision, a materially safer and more reliable workflow than UI clicking.
leverage_evidence: About text names seven tools including document state, clause extraction, assessment, context, and export.
Frames show clause-specific HIGH risk cards, redline markup, and Keep as-is/decision controls.
execution_rationale: The frames demonstrate a coherent flow from 22-page contract loading through risk annotation and explicit redline decisions, though final export is not shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show Page 1 of 22, employment contract content, risk annotations, redlines, and reset/decision controls.
Devpost screenshot shows a dedicated demo video preview and aligned product description.
impact_rationale: People facing complex employment contracts and deadlines have a concrete, high-value need; clause-grounded explanations and actionable negotiation language directly address it.
impact_evidence: About text targets workers with employment offers, deadlines, and expensive legal alternatives.
Frames show a specific five-year worldwide non-compete flagged HIGH with supporting context.
creativity_rationale: The blur-as-progress metaphor and human-by-human clause decisions create a memorable interaction model for a serious document workflow.
creativity_evidence: Description says clauses snap into clarity only after assessment and decisions.
Frames visibly show progressive clarity, redline markup, and contextual issue cards.
usability_note: Strong staged workflow and explicit decisions; legal accuracy and export completion are not verified.
red_flags: Final saved/exported negotiation email is not visibly shown.
standouts: Excellent alignment of tool-level document state with human approval.
Clear visual metaphor tied to actual review state.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed product, impact, and WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Privacy-first support navigator with deterministic rules and auditable agent tools.
what_it_does: Lets humans control sensitive facts while an agent discovers support options, analyzes a structured case, explains choices, compares alternatives, and prepares a checklist.
leverage_rationale: Typed domain tools and shared rule-engine state reduce scraping ambiguity while preserving human authority over sensitive facts; this is more than a convenience wrapper.
leverage_evidence: About text describes six structured tools and a deterministic JS rule engine shared by UI and tools.
Frames show tool inventory, structured case facts, recommendation output, and agent/human workflow panels.

execution_evidence: Frames show six named tools and a Student Stability Bridge recommendation from case facts.
Devpost preview shows Local intent -> Deterministic rules -> WebMCP tools -> Human review architecture.
impact_rationale: People navigating complex public-service support have a real need for understandable, auditable guidance, and the human-controlled privacy model is well matched.
impact_evidence: About text explicitly targets rule-heavy support/public-service websites and sensitive facts.
Frames show case facts, matched/missing conditions, recommendation, and next-step structure.
creativity_rationale: The human-controls-facts/agent-orchestrates model is a thoughtful safety-oriented interaction, though the support navigator category is established.
creativity_evidence: Explicit separation of agent orchestration from eligibility authority.
Shared deterministic engine and visible activity/audit framing.
usability_note: Structured facts and visible recommendations support auditability; real user data flow is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No readable tool-call trace or complete end-to-end interaction in the packet.
advance_reason: Credible public-service use case with strong structured-tool and safety design.

one_line: Private in-browser CSV analysis that returns aggregates without exposing rows.
what_it_does: Parses spending CSVs locally, provides structured aggregate/anomaly tools to an agent, and highlights relevant rows in the user's own table.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables an agent to query sensitive, page-local data while receiving only answers; a normal hosted agent workflow would require exporting raw records, making the privacy capability transformative.
leverage_evidence: About text states CSV parsing/querying/summarization are entirely in-browser and agent receives only answers.
Devpost preview visibly shows 965 rows parsed, Privacy Mode, agent analysis, and browser tooling context.
execution_rationale: The demo evidence shows CSV selection/sample reload, parsed-row status, privacy mode, and concrete anomaly/category output; network-zero claim is described but not independently verified.
execution_evidence: Screenshot/video preview shows Choose a CSV, Reload sample expenses, 965 rows parsed in-browser, and analysis findings.
About text enumerates seven tools and describes row highlighting and per-category anomaly detection.
impact_rationale: Individuals and privacy-conscious analysts have a concrete need to understand financial data without uploading raw transactions; the demonstrated answer-only model directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets sensitive bank statements and payslips.
Demo preview shows unusual-charge findings while Privacy Mode withholds row details.
creativity_rationale: The local-data/answer-only agent pattern is an inventive and memorable application of page-owned tools to sensitive analytics.
creativity_evidence: No-backend architecture is explicitly chosen to preserve the premise.
Rows remain in the user's table while aggregates are exposed to the agent.
usability_note: Clear upload, privacy toggle, and analysis surfaces; arbitrary CSV robustness is not shown.
red_flags: Privacy/network behavior is claimed rather than independently inspectable from stills.
standouts: Excellent WebMCP delta through page-local sensitive data.
advance_reason: Transformative privacy use of WebMCP with strong visible demo evidence.

one_line: Browser-native control plane that discovers tools and gates mutations with human approval.
what_it_does: Binds origins, normalizes provider schemas, runs safe reads, and requires separate human approvals with drift and replay checks before external effects.
leverage_rationale: The product's purpose is structured multi-origin WebMCP orchestration with authority separation; comparable generic UI automation cannot provide the same provenance, nonce, drift, and fail-closed guarantees.
leverage_evidence: About text claims native multi-origin topology, page binding, exact approvals, drift checks, replay protection, and fail-closed dispatch.
Transcript describes separate read/mutation routes, two approval envelopes, receipts, and rejected replay/origin attacks.
execution_rationale: Unlike most packets, a 160-second video transcript describes multiple complete missions, approved mutations with receipts, fallback, and security rejection paths; frames show the control-plane UI, though exact text is small.
execution_evidence: Transcript reports production recovery mission, two approved mutations, receipts, sealed audit, fallback, and three security attacks stopped before dispatch.
Frames show a persistent dark control-plane workspace with panels and state variations.
impact_rationale: Safe agent action across real websites is a broad and important problem; exact human authority and auditable evidence address high-consequence automation risks.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly centers human authority over every mutation.
Transcript describes origin binding, one-time nonce, expiry, recovery path, and auditable rejections.
creativity_rationale: The braid metaphor is realized as a novel cross-origin mission/control model combining discovery, provenance, approvals, recovery, and security testing.
creativity_evidence: Multi-origin mission model maps heterogeneous tools into a common execution plan.
Separate approval envelopes prevent one approval authorizing another.
usability_note: Complex control-plane surface is coherent but dense; usability for ordinary users is uncertain.
red_flags: Frame text is low-resolution; claims rely materially on transcript.
standouts: Demonstrated attack rejection and approved mutation receipts.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP centrality and unusually complete evidence of both success and fail-closed behavior.

standouts: Very high WebMCP leverage for precise geometry/state access.

one_line: Multiplayer classroom canvas with teacher-scoped AI coaching and watch mode.

leverage_rationale: Two-way page/agent communication, shared live canvas state, and teacher-specific skills make the agent a participant in a synchronized classroom rather than a separate chat; generic UI driving is materially less reliable.

Devpost preview visibly shows quadratic problem, learner sticky note, detailed feedback, and generated graph.
impact_rationale: Classrooms need simultaneous collaboration and differentiated feedback; teacher-controlled coaching that handles handwriting and shared context directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: About text identifies students with different speeds and handwritten/diagrammatic work.
Frames show concrete math feedback, generated graph, contextual video, and teacher skill customization.
creativity_rationale: The combination of multiplayer canvas, teacher-portable skills, two-way agent polling, handwriting understanding, and watch-mode differentiated coaching is unusually ambitious and memorable.
